# Exposed contact faces: genuine dimension reduction and the inward trace

This note separates three facts about a fixed continuous normal and an
actual affine supporting plane. The full geometric contact face is a
genuine lower-dimensional mixed body. Its inward collar has an exact
finite-cap signature limit, but this limit is not in general the closed
halfspace trace on the face. Finally, a center of the face has zero depth
for the original mixed volume. These statements do not close OC by
induction.

The ordinary proper-section reduction and its nonuniform-trace obstruction
were already proved in `candidate ce2469e6ba848252`.
The affine-contact face-poset transport and its shared-capacity obstruction
were already proved in
`candidate 6eda5637cc09a539`.
The specific addition here is the exact exposed-face and joint inward-trace
interface; no new global transport or center theorem is claimed.

## 1. The full contact component is an actual mixed body

Let P be a finite, nonempty lattice-complete subset of Z^n, meaning
conv(P) intersect Z^n=P. Let K_z be positive-volume d-dimensional convex
polytopes, d>=1, which are the actual integer fibers of

    C_0=conv union_(z in P) ({z} times K_z).

Thus all anchored Minkowski inclusions at integer bases hold. Write
mu_d(E)=sum_(z in P) vol_d(E_z). Fix a unit continuous normal u and an
affine function ell on aff(P) with

    h_(K_z)(u)<=ell(z) for all z in P.

Its geometric contact face is

    F=C_0 intersect {u.x=ell(z)}.

Put F_z=K_z intersect {u.x=ell(z)}, and let Q be its nonempty integer
fiber base set. Let Q_+ be the indices with positive H_(d-1)(F_z).
For d=1, a nonempty exposed endpoint has H_0 mass one, so Q_+=Q.

**Lemma 1.** Q and, if nonempty, Q_+ are lattice-complete. If Q_+ is
nonempty, after restricting F to conv(Q_+) in base space and applying a
lattice-preserving coordinate change, it is a convex body in
R^m times R^(d-1), where m=dim aff(Q_+). Its mixed (d-1)-volume is exactly

    A=sum_(z in Q_+) H_(d-1)(F_z),                         (1)

with no Jacobian depending on the integer slope of ell. The restriction
retains every positive-measure original face fiber exactly.

Proof. Because the support inequality holds on every generator of C_0,
F is the convex hull of the contact generators. In particular its
projection is conv(Q). If an integer p lies in conv(Q), a convex
combination of points in the corresponding F_z lies in F_p. Thus p is
in Q. If instead p lies in conv(Q_+), a Minkowski combination of the
parallel full-dimensional (d-1)-faces lies in F_p and has positive
(d-1)-volume. This follows either from Brunn--Minkowski in the common
parallel hyperplane or directly by combining contained relative open
balls. Hence p is in Q_+. Both converse containments are immediate.

Rotate continuous coordinates so u=e_d, and write x=(xi,t). The map
(z,xi,t) -> (z,xi,t-ell(z)) preserves Z^n times R^d. On F, its last
coordinate is zero and can be dropped. Within each integer fiber this
map is an isometry on the face: xi are orthonormal tangent coordinates.
This proves the exact measure assertion. It is not a statement about
the ambient surface measure of the sloped face across continuous z.

Choose z_0 in Q_+. The lattice
(aff(Q_+)-z_0) intersect Z^n is saturated and has rank m. A basis of a
saturated sublattice extends to a unimodular basis: split off a primitive
vector using integer Euclidean operations, and induct on its rank.
Consequently an integer translation and unimodular base transformation
send this affine lattice to Z^m times {0}; drop its fixed coordinates.
The continuous tangent coordinate and its measure do not change.
Finally, choose m+1 affinely independent bases and a relative open
(d-1)-ball in each face fiber. Their convex hull has affine dimension
m+d-1, proving nonempty interior in the reduced ambient space.
The case m=d-1=0 is a single point and is handled directly. QED.

For any original closed cap

    H={a.z+v.x>=b},

write c=v.u and v_perp=v-cu. Its exact restriction, before the base
rank reduction, is

    a.z+v_perp.xi+c ell(z)>=b.                            (2)

After rank reduction this is a genuine closed halfspace, the whole
space, or the empty set. An entire fiber on its boundary is retained.
Thus, conditional on OC in continuous dimension d-1, the full geometric
face measure has an actual center at an integer base with its exact
lower-dimensional depth bound. This is a legitimate induction INPUT,
not a statement about a selected weighted boundary stress.

## 2. Exact joint trace of an inward collar

For epsilon>0 let

    L_epsilon=C_0 intersect {ell(z)-epsilon<=u.x<=ell(z)}.

Only its integer fibers are measured. For finitely many fixed ambient
closed caps H_i={a_i.z+v_i.x>=b_i}, put c_i=v_i.u. At a point of F_z
write the face margin as

    A_i(z,xi)=a_i.z+(v_i-c_i u).xi+c_i ell(z)-b_i.

Define the inward bit on F_z by

    I_i^in(z,xi)=1 if A_i(z,xi)>0,
                 1 if A_i(z,xi)=0 and c_i<=0,
                 0 otherwise.                              (3)

Values on a proper tangent cutting hyperplane have no effect on the
face integral. Formula (3) matters on a whole facet coincidence.

**Lemma 2.** For every function Psi:{0,1}^N -> R,

 lim_(epsilon down 0) (1/epsilon)
   integral_(L_epsilon intersect (Z^n times R^d))
       Psi(1_H1,...,1_HN) dmu_d
 =sum_(z in Q_+) integral_(F_z) Psi(I_1^in,...,I_N^in) dH_(d-1).
                                                               (4)

In particular mu_d(L_epsilon)/epsilon -> A. A zero-area exposed face
contributes zero to (4), although it remains part of the geometric face.

Proof. At a fixed contact base use t=ell(z)-u.x>=0 and tangent slice
S_z(t). Its compact slices converge in Hausdorff distance to F_z as
t down 0. One direct proof is as follows. Every limit of points in S_z(t)
belongs to F_z by compactness. Conversely, fix an interior point of K_z
at depth h>0. The slice S_z(t), for 0<t<h, contains the affine image
(1-t/h)F_z+(t/h)xi_*; this approximates F_z. If F_z has positive tangent
volume, these slices have uniformly bounded tangent volume and their
indicators converge almost everywhere to 1_Fz. Their boundaries are
Lebesgue null. If F_z has zero tangent volume, their volumes tend to zero,
by outer containment in arbitrarily thin neighborhoods of F_z. The d=1
case is the same statement for the unique zero-dimensional tangent
point and an interval immediately inside its endpoint.

At depth t the cap margin is exactly A_i(z,xi)-c_i t. If its tangent
part is nonconstant, the equality hyperplane has measure zero and the
cap indicator converges almost everywhere to the usual sign of A_i.
If the tangent part vanishes, A_i is constant on the entire tangent
space. A nonzero constant has its fixed sign for all small t, while a
zero constant gives precisely 1_{c_i<=0} for every t>0. This proves
convergence to (3) simultaneously for all N caps. Psi is bounded because
its domain is finite. Dominated convergence in the bounded tangent box
gives the slice limit, and averaging t from 0 to epsilon gives (4).
At a noncontact base the positive gap ell(z)-h_z excludes that entire
fiber for all sufficiently small epsilon. Finally sum over the finitely
many bases. QED.

For one cap, the difference from the usual CLOSED face trace is exactly

 sum_(z in Q_+: A_i(z,.) identically 0 and c_i>0) H_(d-1)(F_z).   (5)

Thus no uniform replacement of (4) by the closed geometric trace is
valid. Likewise, varying caps may have coefficients on the scale
1/epsilon and require a further tangent blowup analysis; Lemma 2 concerns
fixed caps only.

## 3. An exact positive-budget joint-signature obstruction

Take n=1,d=2 and

    C=[-1,1]_z times [0,1]_s times [-1,0]_t,
    u=e_t, ell=0, P={-1,0,1}.

The contact face has three unit intervals. The caps

    H_+={t+z>=0},   H_-={-t+z>=0},   H_0={-z>=0}

have positive original mixed areas 1,2,2 respectively. Their union
covers the full continuous fiber plane at every base: at z<=0 the last
cap suffices; at z=1 the first two already cover all t.

On F the first two caps have the IDENTICAL closed restriction z>=0.
In particular each captures face mass two. For 0<epsilon<1, however,

    mu_2(L_epsilon intersect H_+)/epsilon=1,
    mu_2(L_epsilon intersect H_-)/epsilon=2.

At the middle face fiber, the closed three-bit signature is (1,1,1),
whereas the inward signature is (0,1,1). The inward intersection credit
of H_+ and H_- is one, while the closed face intersection mass is two.
All these equalities are exact, without a limiting error. This is an
actual convex polytope with a lattice-complete base and uniform full
face measure. It is not claimed to be a below-target critical circuit.
It disproves identification of closed face profiles with inward cap
losses even for positive-budget covering caps.

## 4. A face center is not an original center

Every y in F intersect (Z^n times R^d) belongs to the ambient closed
supporting cap {u.x>=ell(z)}. This cap captures only exposed faces in
the original fibers, hence has original mixed d-volume zero. Therefore

    depth_(original mixed d-volume)(y)=0.                  (6)

An inductively selected center in F is an actual mixed point, but (6)
prevents it from serving directly as the original positive-depth center.
Transverse displacement needs a new all-cap volume argument; the mere
existence of a lower-dimensional center does not provide one.

There is also no automatic replacement of Gamma_d by Gamma_(d-1) for
convex boundary-profile payment. The existing sharp simplex-facet theorem
already rules this out. In its elementary planar instance, take a
triangle and its three canonical centroid caps with response weights
1/3. On one edge, parametrized by s in [0,1], their profile is

    W(s)=1/3 on [0,1/3) union (2/3,1],
         2/3 on [1/3,2/3].

Its exact convex-potential optimum is 4/9, not Gamma_1=1/2. Indeed
W-4/9 has zero mass and first moment, is positive on the middle interval,
and negative on the two ends. For any convex phi, subtract the secant
through 1/3 and 2/3. The remaining function is nonpositive in the middle
and nonnegative on the ends, so

    integral phi W <= (4/9) integral phi.

Constant phi attains equality. These are genuine globally critical
ordinary caps. This calibration is an illustration of the archived
all-dimensional facet theorem, not a new counterexample.

## 5. What survives, and what is still missing

The legitimate lower-dimensional object is the FULL contact face of
Lemma 1, after its positive-measure base reduction. The normal-preserving
stress need not restrict to its uniform measure. Its target capacity can
be shared by several affine-contact faces, as in the archived face-poset
example. A selected subdensity is not repaired by lattice completeness.

Even for the full geometric face, Lemma 2 requires the inward bits and
(6) requires an actual lift of the center. The fixed-normal facet
dimension drop therefore supplies a genuine geometric body and exact
trace formulas, but not a new global cap-budget implication beyond the
archived normal-convex-order constraints. Reopening this induction route
needs a quantitative transverse source/loss argument retaining (3),
shared contact capacities, and the original d-volume denominator.
